Their Voices reaching Far Distant Places
Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s Voice Reaches Far into the Distance and is Heard by Hadhrat Saariyah (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once dispatched an army, he appointed someone by the name of Hadhrat Saariyah (RA) as its commander. Hadhrat Umar (RA) was one day delivering a lecture when he suddenly called out, "The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!" This he called out three times. When a messenger from the same later arrived (in Madinah), Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him for a report. He said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! We were being defeated when we suddenly heard a voice thrice calling out, "The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!" We then put our backs towards the mountain, as a result of which Allaah defeated the enemy." Someone then said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "It was you who shouted out that command."[^2]

In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that while Hadhrat Umar (RA) was delivering a sermon, he suddenly called out, "The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain! The one who makes a wolf the shepherd of a flock has truly committed a grave injustice." The people looked at each other in surprise, but Hadhrat Ali (RA) assured them that Hadhrat Umar (RA) will surely have an explanation for what he had said. When they questioned Hadhrat Umar (RA) after he had completed, he explained, "The vision flashed through my mind that the Mushrikeen would defeat our brothers who were then passing by a mountain. If they turned towards the mountain (placing it at their backs), they would have to fight from one direction only (allowing them to win a victory). However, if they passed by the mountain, they would be destroyed (because they would have to fight the enemy from the direction of the mountain as well). What you claim to have heard me say is my response to that situation."
A month later, someone (from the Muslim army) came with the good news that they had heard Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s voice that day, because of which they turned towards the mountain and were granted a victory by Allaah.[^3]

Another narration states that the people asked Hadhrat Ali (RA), "Did you hear Umar (RA) say, 'O Saariyah!' while he was delivering the lecture on the pulpit?" "Shame on you people!" Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Leave Umar alone because he always has a valid explanation for anything he does."[^4]
Bayhaqi, Laalkaa'i in Sharhus Sunnah, Zain Aaqooli in his Fawaa'id and Ibnul A'raabi in his Karaamaatul Awliyaa, as quoted by Harmala in his Jam'u.
Ibn Mardway, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.3). Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il (Pg.210) and Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami in his Arba'een have reported a similar narration.
Khateeb and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.386). Allaama Ibn Katheer has commented on the authenticity of the narration in his Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.7 Pg.131).
